title: Affine normalization charts via total fractions without a Noetherian hypothesis
statement:
Let $X$ be a reduced scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme] such that every quasi-compact open has finitely many irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Let $
u:X^
u	o X$ be the componentwise normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization], and let $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ be an affine open [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $S_A$ be the multiplicative set of nonzerodivisors of $A$ (elements $s$ for which $sa=0$ implies $a=0$), put $Q(A)=S_A^{-1}A$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], and let $\overline A\subseteq Q(A)$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $Q(A)$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Then $A$ is reduced and has finitely many minimal prime ideals (prime ideals containing no strictly smaller prime ideal), and there is a canonical isomorphism $
u^{-1}(U)\simeq\operatorname{Spec}\overline A$ over $U$. Under this isomorphism the structural ring map is $A	o\overline A$, $a\mapsto a/1$. No Noetherian or finiteness-of-normalization hypothesis is imposed. If $U$ is empty, $A$, $Q(A)$ and $\overline A$ are the zero ring and both schemes in this isomorphism are empty.

source.place: Tag 035P, label lemma-description-normalization, parts (1) and (4); componentwise normalization is the same normalization by Tag 0CDV, label lemma-normalization-in-terms-of-components.

proof.text: By [def-pc-reduced-scheme], $A=\mathcal O_X(U)$ is reduced. Apply [lem-sfb-normalization-generic-residue-affine-charts] to $X,U$: it provides the finite set $I_U$ of generic points of the components of $U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes], those components are the $V(\mathfrak p_i)$ for the minimal primes $\mathfrak p_i$ of $A$. Distinct minimal primes give distinct closed sets: $V(\mathfrak p)$ contains $\mathfrak q$ precisely when $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak q$. Their generic points are the points $\mathfrak p_i$ themselves, since the closure of $\{\mathfrak p_i\}$ is $V(\mathfrak p_i)$. Thus we can index all the minimal primes without repetition by this finite set.

Apply [lem-sfb-reduced-weakass-minimal] to the reduced ring $A$. Every weakly associated prime is one of the finitely many $\mathfrak p_i$ from step 1. Therefore [lem-sc-affine-totalquotient-minimal-product] gives the canonical isomorphism $\alpha:Q(A)\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_i A_{\mathfrak p_i}$. Its $i$-th coordinate sends $a/s$ to $(a/1)(s/1)^{-1}$, so it is compatible with the maps from $A$. This application requires only finiteness of the minimal primes and the weakly associated prime condition, both now established.

source.place: Tag 035P (lemma-description-normalization), proof of (2); Algebra Tags 0EMA and 02LX.

proof.text: For each $i$, [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-reduced-localization-field] gives $\mathfrak p_iA_{\mathfrak p_i}=0$ and says $A_{\mathfrak p_i}$ is a field. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], the isomorphism $A_{\mathfrak p_i}\simeq\mathcal O_{X,\eta_i}$ sends $a/s$ to $a_{\eta_i}s_{\eta_i}^{-1}$, where $\eta_i$ is the corresponding point of $U$. Its quotient by the maximal ideal therefore identifies $A_{\mathfrak p_i}$ with $\kappa_X(\eta_i)$, using the residue-field definition [def-weil-residue-field]. Compose these coordinate isomorphisms with $\alpha$ to obtain an $A$-algebra isomorphism $e:Q(A)\xrightarrow{\sim}C_U=\prod_i\kappa_X(\eta_i)$. Explicitly $e(a/1)$ is the tuple of residue classes of the germs of $a$, exactly the $A$-algebra structure required by the chart lemma.

source.place: Tag 035P (lemma-description-normalization), proof of (2); Algebra Tag 00EU; Schemes Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), (6).

proof.text: Write $D_U\subseteq C_U$ for the integral closure in [lem-sfb-normalization-generic-residue-affine-charts]. The isomorphism $e$ restricts to $\bar e:\overline A\xrightarrow{\sim}D_U$: if $z$ satisfies a monic equation $z^n+\sum_{j<n}(a_j/1)z^j=0$, applying $e$ gives the same monic equation for $e(z)$, since $e(a_j/1)$ is the structural image of $a_j$. Conversely apply $e^{-1}$ to a monic equation for an element of $D_U$. This is precisely integrality as defined in [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Apply the contravariant spectrum functor [def-weil-affine-spectrum] to $\bar e$ and compose $\nu^{-1}(U)\simeq\operatorname{Spec}D_U$ from the chart lemma with $\operatorname{Spec}(\bar e):\operatorname{Spec}D_U\simeq\operatorname{Spec}\overline A$. The composite is over $U$: on rings, $a$ maps to $e(a/1)$ in $D_U$ and then to $a/1$ in $\overline A$. All maps used are the canonical localization, germ, residue and integral-closure maps, so the identification is canonical.

source.place: Tag 035P (lemma-description-normalization), (4), and Tag 0CDV (lemma-normalization-in-terms-of-components); transport of integral closure along the canonical algebra isomorphism.

proof.text: If $U$ is empty, its ring of sections $A$ is the zero ring by the sheaf axiom for the empty open. In the localization $Q(A)=S_A^{-1}A$, $0=1$ still holds, so $Q(A)$ is the zero ring [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Its integral-closure subring $\overline A$ is also the zero ring [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Its spectrum has no prime ideals [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The chart lemma [lem-sfb-normalization-generic-residue-affine-charts] states that the inverse image of this empty $U$ is empty. Thus the preceding isomorphism has exactly the asserted empty-case interpretation.

proof_origin.place: Tag 035P (lemma-description-normalization), proof of (1), (2), (4), with the componentwise formulation of Tag 0CDV and Algebra Tag 0EMA.

lean.statement: theorem normalization_affine_total_fractions (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsReduced X] (hfinite : ∀ V : X.Opens, IsCompact (V : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents V).Finite) (U : X.affineOpens) : _root_.IsReduced Γ(X, U) ∧ (minimalPrimes Γ(X, U)).Finite ∧ (∃ e : (X.fromReducedNormalization ⁻¹ᵁ U.1).toScheme ≅ Spec (.of (integralClosure Γ(X, U) (Localization (nonZeroDivisors Γ(X, U))))), e.hom ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap Γ(X, U) (integralClosure Γ(X, U) (Localization (nonZeroDivisors Γ(X, U)))))) ≫ U.2.isoSpec.inv = X.fromReducedNormalization ∣_ U.1) ∧ (U.1 = ⊥ → Subsingleton Γ(X, U) ∧ Subsingleton (Localization (nonZeroDivisors Γ(X, U))) ∧ Subsingleton (integralClosure Γ(X, U) (Localization (nonZeroDivisors Γ(X, U)))) ∧ IsEmpty (X.fromReducedNormalization ⁻¹ᵁ U.1).toScheme ∧ IsEmpty (Spec (.of (integralClosure Γ(X, U) (Localization (nonZeroDivisors Γ(X, U)))))))
